projectDir.description: Directory holding the project, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.

version-declared.name: Go version is declared
version-declared.description: The module declares the Go version it is built against, and that version is no older than the configured floor.
version-declared.remediation:
Declare the Go version the module builds against in `go.mod`:

```
go 1.22
```

`go mod edit -go=1.22` writes it for you. Without the directive, the language version is whatever the toolchain defaults to, so a build can accept syntax on one runner and reject it on another. A module far below the floor is compiled by a toolchain that is no longer supported.

minVersion.description: Oldest Go version accepted. A declared version below this is a violation.

checksums-committed.name: Go module checksums are committed
checksums-committed.description: The module commits `go.sum`, so every module a build downloads is verified against the checksum recorded in the commit.
checksums-committed.remediation:
Commit the checksum file the Go tooling writes:

```bash
go mod tidy
git add go.sum
```

`go.sum` holds the checksum of every module in the dependency graph. Without it, nothing verifies that what the build downloaded is what the module authors published, so a swapped or rewritten version reaches the binary unnoticed.

no-local-replacements.name: No module is replaced by a directory
no-local-replacements.description: No `replace` directive points a module at a filesystem path, so the build only uses source that is in the checkout.
no-local-replacements.remediation:
Remove the directive and require the module by its own path, or replace it with a module path and version instead of a directory:

```
replace github.com/company/queue => github.com/company/queue/v2 v2.1.0
```

For local development across several modules, list the directories in the `use` block of a `go.work` file instead of adding another `replace`:

```
go 1.22

use (
	./widget
	./queue
)
```

A `replace` that points at a directory builds from something the checkout doesn't contain, so it compiles on the author's laptop and nowhere else.

toolchain-pinned.name: Go toolchain is pinned
toolchain-pinned.description: The module names the exact toolchain that compiles it, instead of leaving the `go` directive as a minimum version.
toolchain-pinned.remediation:
Name the toolchain next to the `go` directive:

```
go 1.22

toolchain go1.22.3
```

`go mod edit -toolchain=go1.22.3` writes it for you. The `go` directive sets the lowest Go version the module builds with, not the one it is built by. Without a toolchain line, the compiler is whichever Go the runner happens to have, and a compiler change arrives without warning.
